title: Azure AI Search: enforce Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels at indexing and query time
summary: The configuration, privileged roles, preview limitations and query-outage behaviour are supported by Microsoft documentation. The title overstates indexing-time enforcement, which is not documented, and the audit navigation note should acknowledge the different route in the feature guide.

claims.claim: Azure AI Search enforces sensitivity labels at indexing time as well as query time.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure AI Search Purview sensitivity labels indexing time enforce access rights query time. Opened search-indexer-sensitivity-labels and search-query-sensitivity-labels: indexing extracts content and metadata; enforcement is described at query time.
claims.fix: Replace the title with "Azure AI Search: ingest Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and enforce them at query time".

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn now names the service Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search).
claims.quote: Query-time enforcement of Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels in Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) (preview)

claims.claim: An indexer can ingest Purview sensitivity label metadata from documents.
claims.quote: The indexer extracts document content and sensitivity-label metadata.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Ordinary label-enforced queries filter results by the requesting user's sensitivity label permissions.
claims.quote: It applies access filters based on Purview policies to return only results the requesting user is allowed to access.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Label-aware indexing and enforcement require administrator configuration rather than automatically changing existing indexes.
claims.quote: If your existing index doesn't have `purviewEnabled: true`, create a new Purview-enabled index and retarget your indexer and any projection selectors to it. You can't enable this property on an existing index.

claims.claim: The service identity needs privileged role grants before this feature can work.
claims.quote: Verify that the Foundry IQ service has its **system-assigned managed identity** (not a user-assigned managed identity) enabled and that it holds the `Content.SuperUser` and `UnifiedPolicy.Tenant.Read` role assignments.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft calls label metadata access highly privileged and asks for security or compliance approval before assigning permissions.
claims.quote: Accessing Microsoft Purview sensitivity label metadata involves highly privileged operations. Engage your security or compliance teams and obtain approval through your organization's governance process before assigning permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Source label changes are not reflected in the index until a successful indexer run processes them.
claims.quote: The index doesn't reflect label changes on source documents until the next successful indexer run.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: purviewEnabled must be true when the index is created and cannot be changed afterwards.
claims.quote: The `purviewEnabled` property must be set to `true` when the index is created. This setting is permanent and can't be modified later.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Why it matters
claims.claim: An existing index without purviewEnabled must be replaced with a new Purview-enabled index and the indexer retargeted.
claims.quote: If your existing index doesn't have `purviewEnabled: true`, create a new Purview-enabled index and retarget your indexer and any projection selectors to it. You can't enable this property on an existing index.

claims.claim: Elevated read bypasses the requesting user's per-document label permissions.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ skips the per-document label-based access check and returns matching documents, regardless of the requesting user's `EXTRACT` permissions on each label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Elevated read emits one Microsoft Purview audit entry for every returned document.
claims.quote: For each document in the response, Foundry IQ emits one entry to the Microsoft Purview audit log on behalf of the requesting tenant. A single search request that returns *N* documents produces *N* audit entries.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; controls[2].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: This feature supports only the search service's system-assigned managed identity, not a user-assigned identity.
claims.quote: The Foundry IQ service must use its **system-assigned managed identity** to authenticate with Microsoft Purview. This feature doesn't support user-assigned managed identities.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles; controls[2].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The feature guide calls for a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator to grant the Purview roles.
claims.quote: Once approved, engage a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator to assign these roles to the Foundry IQ system-assigned managed identity:

claims.claim: The service and querying user must belong to the same Microsoft Entra tenant.
claims.quote: Both the Foundry IQ service and the user issuing the query must be in the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Purview-enabled indexes require RBAC authentication and do not accept API-key document operations.
claims.quote: Purview-enabled indexes require RBAC authentication for document operations, including indexing content and querying. Keep both RBAC and API keys enabled if other service operations rely on API keys. This configuration doesn't permit API-key document operations on Purview-enabled indexes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Ordinary label-enforced queries require the delegated user token in addition to the application's RBAC authorisation.
claims.quote:
The delegated user identity, provided in the `x-ms-query-source-authorization` header.

Both are required to authorize label-based visibility.

claims.claim: During a Purview outage, a non-elevated call without x-ms-query-source-authorization from an application with at least Search Index Data Reader can succeed with unlabelled-only results.
claims.quote: **Calls without `x-ms-query-source-authorization`** issued by an application with at least the **Search Index Data Reader** role: The request succeeds and returns only documents that don't have a sensitivity label. Labeled documents are omitted from the response.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Microsoft limits the intended use of the unlabelled-only degraded path to non-user-facing workflows.
claims.quote: This degraded path is intended only for non-user-facing workflows that explicitly accept unlabeled-only results. Don't rely on it for end-user search experiences.

claims.claim: Standard label-enforced requests fail with a 5xx error when Purview cannot be reached instead of returning partial or unfiltered results.
claims.quote: **Standard label-enforced requests** (with `x-ms-query-source-authorization`): The request fails with `5xx`. Foundry IQ doesn't return partial or unfiltered results when it can't evaluate label policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Azure preview terms apply to this feature.
claims.quote: Query-time enforcement of Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels is in Public Preview and is subject to the Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing

claims.quote: Enabling extraction, adding metadata fields, or retargeting the pipeline doesn't make unchanged files eligible for a normal incremental run. To reprocess those files, reset the indexer, then run it.

claims.claim: The feature guides do not specify which Purview or Microsoft 365 licence is required specifically for label-aware Azure AI Search.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview service description "Azure AI Search" sensitivity labels license. Read indexer/query prerequisites, Purview sensitivity-label licensing and service-description search excerpts; no Azure AI Search-specific Purview SKU is stated.

claims.claim: Purview publishes general sensitivity label licensing and billing requirements that should be consulted separately.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use. Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Source file types must be supported by both Purview sensitivity labels and the search indexers.
claims.quote: Use source documents with file types that are both supported by Purview sensitivity labels and supported by Foundry IQ indexers.

claims.claim: Elevated read requires Search Index Data Contributor at the service or index scope.
claims.quote: The calling developer user must hold the **Search Index Data Contributor** role on the Foundry IQ service or index scope. **Search Index Data Reader** isn't sufficient.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Foundry IQ record type in Purview audit search can be used to investigate elevated read activity.
claims.quote:
Foundry IQ uploads audit entries to the calling tenant's Microsoft Purview audit log. To investigate elevated read activity:

1. In the Microsoft Purview portal, select **Solutions** > **Audit**.
2. Select **Audit Search**, and then filter by date range, user, or the Foundry IQ record type.
